description: What a third party can actually re-run, per checked-in corpus. This file is the machine-readable source for docs/benchmarks/reproducible-corpora.md; a test asserts every corpus in benchmarks/ appears exactly once, that every declared case count matches the file, and that every named command points at a script that exists.
privacy: no recordings, no personal dictation, and no private user state is referenced by any clone-only corpus

requirement_classes.clone-only: Runs with nothing but a git clone and uv. No network, no downloads, no personal data, no hardware beyond the machine running it.
requirement_classes.needs-download: Requires a public dataset or model download before it can run.
requirement_classes.needs-local-service: Requires a locally running service such as Ollama with a pulled model.
requirement_classes.needs-apple-silicon: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac and installed runtime assets.
requirement_classes.needs-external-observations: Requires observation files a human must collect outside this repository.
requirement_classes.needs-private-runtime-log: Requires a log produced by actually dictating on an installed machine.
requirement_classes.reference-data: Not a case corpus; thresholds, pins, or protocol definitions consumed by another command.

corpora.notes: The golden-corpus half is fully reproducible. The optional --transcripts telemetry half reads private local dictation history and degrades to 'unavailable' for anyone else, which is the correct outcome, not a failure.
Synthetic classification and selector policy only. The artifact states that no audio, verifier, runtime ASR backend, or physical device was exercised.
Adapter simulation only. The report prints zero real apps exercised. Its capability profiles are also the reference corpus for the physical app-matrix capture harness.
point_and_speak_resolver.py has no CLI of its own, so the public scorecard is the reproducing command.
drop_to_target.py has no CLI of its own. There is no drag path in the codebase at all; these cases only decide whether a named target could accept one.

Coverage of the accent, noise, and quiet-speech dimensions passes on scenario labels only. Those cases carry explicit unfulfilled recording requirements; a text fixture cannot prove acoustic performance. The lifecycle and stress commands read the same corpus and are also clone-only.

Every observation is 'unavailable' with reason 'not_run'. It exists so a third party can execute the evaluator end to end and see the output shape without collecting anything. It contains no measurement by construction, and a test enforces that.

The latency path needs a local Ollama serving the pinned cleanup model, and refuses to start without --run. The proof-recovery half of the same corpus IS clone-only: uv run benchmark_cleanup_proof_recovery.py.

The protocol is reproducible; the runs are not. Producing a real observation file needs clean machines, the other products, and a human observer. The corpus itself declares product_results_included: false.

Ranking the checked-in evidence is clone-only. Regenerating the metrics needs a LibriSpeech download, an Apple Silicon Mac, the MLX snapshots, and the installed Parakeet helper. uv run performance_lab.py audit-models additionally needs network access to the public Hugging Face API.

Only the ci_warm_path profile is reachable from a clone. The product_quality, warm_path_stage, and startup_readiness profiles all need private runtime logs produced by actually dictating on an installed machine.
Self-describing. The test that reads it is the thing that keeps this file honest.

Pinned deterministic quality metrics, not a corpus: the release gate replays the golden, scorecard, proof-recovery and stress collectors and fails on any difference. --rebaseline rewrites it; the diff rides the causing PR.
